title: OMAC: A Holistic Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
claim: An iterative loop initializes candidates, evaluates them through collaboration, contrasts good and bad ones, and feeds improvements back.
layout: Single row of stages left-to-right with a return loop below
description: A cyclic workflow diagram drawn with dashed arrows. At top left, a blue robot icon labeled Semantic Initializer feeds a yellow rounded panel of Initialized Agents/Controllers, shown as three orange agent icons separated by vertical dots. Dashed arrows lead from each icon into a blue panel labeled Collaboration, which holds server-stack icons. More arrows lead to a peach panel labeled Performance Scores, which holds code-bracket icons. A dark green dashed arrow exits right toward the bottom row. There, a green-bordered box shows Positive vs Negative agent icons. This box feeds a second blue robot, the Contrastive Comparator. A gray arrow then leads to the Optimized Agent/Controller icon, and an upward arrow returns it to the initialized agents. The eye goes first to the pastel panels at top.
caption: OMAC workflow for a single dimension.
abstract: Agents powered by advanced large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities across diverse complex applications. Recently, Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), wherein multiple agents collaborate and communicate with each other, have exhibited enhanced capabilities in complex tasks, such as high-quality code generation and arithmetic reasoning. However, the development of such systems often relies on handcrafted methods, and the literature on systematic design and optimization of LLM-based MAS remains limited. In this work, we introduce \textbf{OMAC}, a general framework designed for holistic optimization of LLM-based MAS. Specifically, we identify five key optimization dimensions for MAS, encompassing both agent functionality and collaboration structure. Building upon these dimensions, we first propose a general algorithm, utilizing two actors termed the Semantic Initializer and the Contrastive Comparator, to optimize any single dimension. Then, we present an algorithm for joint optimization across multiple dimensions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of OMAC on diverse tasks against recent approaches.
